results.name: Medallion for a beadwork necklace
results.description:
The medallion is a reworked silver coin from 1765. This is a typical decorative element which was used only with beads and the image that was the most popular in Podhale was the one of Empress Maria Theresa. One side of the presented medallion features an image of the Mother of God wearing a crown, with a sceptre in Her right hand. The Madonna supports a sitting Infant Jesus, who is holding an apple, with her left hand. An inscription that reads PATRONA BAVARIAE and the year 1765 runs along the inner rim of the coin. The reverse of the medallion shows a bust of the Bavarian elector Maximilian III Joseph Wittelsbach (1727–1777) as a long-haired man in profile. 

ID no.: E/8243/MT

Time of creation: 1765 (coin), before 1979 (medaillon)

Museum: The Dr. Tytus Chałubiński Tatra Museum in Zakopane

https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/1799

results.name: Bust of Queen Nefertiti
results.description: Representation of the iconic bust of Queen Nefertiti. The model captures her serene and regal expression, with her head held high and her eyes gently looking ahead. The queen's tall, intricately designed blue crown is adorned with golden, red, and green details, which are characteristic of her royal attire. The bust also includes the famous golden necklace, finely sculpted facial features, and detailed texture of her skin. The subtle lighting highlights the smooth contours of the sculpture, emphasizing the balance between realism and artistic interpretation.

results.name: Terracotta Bust - Mesoamerica
results.description:
Hand-modeled from terracotta, it showcases stylized facial features, wide eyes, and an elaborate headdress typical of Gulf Coast Mesoamerican art. The figure prominently wears a beaded necklace and holds a u-shaped object, which likely represents a ritual yoke used in the Mesoamerican ballgame. Artifacts like this were highly significant in spiritual practices, serving vital functions in ancestral veneration and agricultural fertility ceremonies.

3D model made using Artec Space Spider.

This work is part of the collaboration agreement between Global Digital Heritage and the Museum of Archaeology, Paleontology, and Science (MAPS). We thank the museum staff at MAPS for their collaboration and efforts.

results.description:

results.name: Dama de Elche
results.description:
3D print model and gamemodel (fbx)
stl file, chitubox file, fbx file (hig and low poly) Textures 2K

The Lady of Elche is an Iberian limestone sculpture made between the 5th and 4th centuries BC. C .. It is a bust that represents a richly dressed lady, whose face shows perfect features. On her head she wears a headdress composed of a tiara covered by a veil, a diadem on her forehead and, on the sides, two buns that frame the face and in which the hairstyle would be collected.

The back and shoulders are covered with a cloak that, on the front, reveals three necklaces with ampholes and amulets, earrings with plates and infulae on the sides of the face and a fibula that closes the tunic. On the back it has a hole that suggests its possible use as a funeral urn. It was originally polychrome and with eyes filled with vitreous paste.

results.name: Dama de Elche
results.description: This model has been taken from the Lady of Elche. The Lady of Elche is one of the most representative sculptures of ancient Iberian art. It was discovered in 1897 at the archaeological site of La Alcudia, near the city of Elche. It is a female bust carved in limestone, dated to around the 4th century BC, notable for its detailed headdress that frames the face with large lateral coils. The figure also wears complex necklaces and ornaments that reflect the high artistic level of Iberian culture. This model was captured through photogrammetry and optimized by Artmonite during a visit to Madrid in 2026. More models in: https://artmonite.com/

results.name: Votive in the form of a Togatus
results.description:
**Collection:** Roman Archeology Dept.
 
**Inv.-No.:** [CAR-M-4006](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1353938)

**Material:** Lead

**Dimensions:** 4,5 x 3,3 cm

**Dating:** 1st-2nd century AD

Bust of a man wearing a toga with distinctive facial features: almond-shaped eyes with circular pupils, a broad, long nose, and pouch-like lips; ears positioned on the sides. He has short hair and is clean-shaven. The folds of the toga fall over the right shoulder, where they are secured with a circular fibula. The collar is edged and may originate from an undergarment or necklace. The back is smooth. The lower edge area is partially broken.

This object was digitized through the 'Kulturerbe digital' program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Bagong – Javanese Wayang Punakawan 3D Character
results.description:
A detailed 3D character portrait of Bagong, one of the iconic Punakawan characters in traditional Javanese Wayang culture.

The model features Bagong's distinctive round face, chubby cheeks, expressive eyes, broad mischievous smile, traditional Javanese head ornament, tied black hair, earrings, wooden-bead necklace, gold pendant, and black-and-gold traditional costume.

Designed with a stylized realistic appearance while preserving the humorous and friendly personality of Bagong. Ideal for 3D rendering, animation, game assets, digital sculpting, collectible statues, cultural visualization, and 3D printing.

results.name: Female Figurine
results.description:
Orange-colored anthropomorphic figurine representing a seated woman with her legs open, nude and with an exposed bust. She has incised hair, punctuated eyes, arms resting at the waist, a visible navel, and open legs. She wears only circular earflares and a necklace of spherical beads. The registration record indicates that this piece dates to the Middle Classic period (A.D. 400–600) and originates from the Tiquisate region, Escuintla.

 IDAEH Cultural Property No. 1.2.144.1308
 
www.fundacionrutamaya.org

Special thanks to the staff of La Ruta Maya Foundation for their hard work on this project.

3D model made using Artec Space Spider

results.name: Woman with Zoomorphic Mask Figurine/Whistle
results.description:
Anthropomorphic figurine depicting a woman with a prominent bust, seated, and holding a round fan in her right hand. She wears a zoomorphic mask, and her forehead features two decorative bands made using a scarification technique. She wears a huipil with a wide neckline, round earspools, a braided necklace, and wrist ornaments. The figurine has a transverse perforation across the shoulders, possibly for suspension.

Cultural Property No. 16.2.5.0051
